1Purpose

This policy is the frame for every specialist disability accommodation () matter at [Provider name]. It names the four thread policies that carry our commitments, and the few rules that bind all of them. It protects the 's rights, their home and their choice of .

2Applies to

  • [Provider name] as a registered NDIS provider of SDA, whether SDA is our only class of supports or one of several.
  • Every we own, lease or manage for SDA, and every dwelling we apply to enrol. This covers every participant who lives in one or is offered a place. A prospective participant has the same rights as a participant (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2)).
  • Everyone who works at or for a dwelling: employees, contractors, tradespeople, agents and volunteers.
  • A participant who provides SDA to themselves. The agreement rule in POL-SDA-03 does not apply to them (, section 9(3)). The dwelling rules do.
  • Our own supported independent living in an SDA dwelling. POL-SIL-05, POL-SIL-02, POL-SIL-03 and POL-SUP-03 apply as well.
  • Our two roles, as landlord and as support provider to the same participant. Every commitment applies to both.

3Commitments

Each commitment below points to the thread policy that carries it. The thread policy's numbers, roles and records are the only source of truth; this policy restates none of them.

C1

We will do what POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: each participant's rights at home, their privacy, and every request to change their dwelling.

C2

We will do what the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) commits to, applied to SDA through PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation): every interest we hold is declared, and a participant's home never depends on their choice of supports.

C3

We will do what POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: a written agreement with every participant, in the terms the law requires.

C4

We will do what POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy commits to: kept within their enrolment, lawful, safe and in good repair.

C5

We will do what POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: fair vacancies, documented arrangements with each SIL provider, and tenancy notices that follow the law.

4Ground rules

The thread policies carry their own ground rules. These four are the ones no thread policy carries, and they bind every SDA procedure.

G1

Every participant has a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share one (, section 24(1)(d)). A participant who chooses to share must tell the in writing, and the NDIA must be satisfied that their needs are not harmed; a notice alone is not the end of it. We help them do it (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)).

G2

Where we own or manage the dwelling, we lead on the dwelling, its repairs and its vacancies. A SIL provider leads on the supports it delivers. Where a matter involves both, the arrangement under AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement names one lead, and both act together.

G3

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, with a written delegation that covers every task the thread policies and procedures give that person. The is not a relative or business associate of the sole trader, has access to REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register, REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register and the register (REG-GOV-02), and is briefed on PRO-SDA-03 and PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) before acting.

G4

If we will miss a time we promised a participant, we tell them before it passes, with the reason and the new date. A time the law sets cannot be moved.

9Words we use

567 words
SDA agreement
the written agreement between us and a participant about their home.
dwelling
a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
participant
a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one.
tenant
a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there.
eligible participant
a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11).
other supports
every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management.
supported independent living (SIL)
help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible.
design category and building type
the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types.
density limit
a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31).
conflict of interest
a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could.
security of tenure
a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end.
tenancy law
the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry.
notice to vacate
a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home.
tenancy action
a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate.
urgent defect
a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit.
independent advocate
a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them.
independent contact
in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO.
NDIS Commission
the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators
short names for the instruments in Authority.

4Ground rules

These rules bind every procedure under this policy.

G1

Nobody is treated worse for reporting a defect, asking for a repair, complaining or declining entry. A defect, a refusal or a complaint is never a reason to end a tenancy or to change a support.

G2

Housing and supports are separate. We never cut, withhold or change a support to affect a person's home. We never use a person's home to affect their supports.

G3

A resident's home is theirs. We enter only with lawful notice and the resident's agreement, or in an emergency that the law allows.

G4

Nothing in this policy authorises a restrictive practice. A lock, gate, sensor or barrier that limits a resident's movement or access may be one. It needs the authorisation the law requires (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support Rules 2018, section 6(e)).

G5

We pay for the repairs and upkeep that the law puts on us. We never charge a resident for fair wear and tear, or for a feature the design category needs. Tenancy law decides when a resident pays for damage they cause.

G6

We sign nothing for the NDIA that we cannot prove. If we find that something we certified was wrong, the Chief Executive acts the same day. They take advice and tell the NDIA in writing within 5 business days (our standard; where the error means the dwelling is no longer suitable, or its circumstances are likely to change, it is also an event under SDA Rules 2020, section 29(1)(b) or (c)).

G7

Each fact is kept once. REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register holds dwelling facts. REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register holds tenancy facts. A resident's personal details and words stay on their own file.

G8

Nobody checks only their own work. A second person re-inspects a sample of dwellings each year.

G9

Where a law of the state or territory is stricter than a time limit in this policy, the law applies.

G10

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds every role in this policy, and names an in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. 1Purpose

The result: every we enrol meets the requirements the enrolled it on. It stays within them. It is safe, secure, private and in good repair.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of Properties Policy, C1 to C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure when any of these happens:

  • we think about enrolling a dwelling
  • a person is offered a home in an
  • an inspection, a certificate or a service falls due
  • a worker, a , the owner or another provider reports a
  • something happens that the NDIA must be told about, or the NDIA writes to us
  • the check of the falls due every 12 months, or the law changes; or the report to the governing body falls due every 3 months
  • the sample re-inspection falls due every 12 months.

Who acts:

  • The opens each dwelling record, checks the dwelling, applies to the NDIA, inspects, rates and chases repairs, and tells the NDIA. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
  • The is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. They tell residents, give notice of entry and warn the SDA Manager of each planned move-in. In a small provider the SDA Manager is the Tenancy Officer.
  • The Quality Manager checks the evidence before a certification, reviews the laws, re-inspects a sample and reports to the governing body.
  • The Chief Executive signs each certification to the NDIA, answers NDIA notices and decides when an enrolment may end.
  • Every worker reports each defect the same day.
  • The on-call manager makes an safe after hours.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader names an in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. That person checks the evidence at step 11 before the sole trader signs at step 12. They do the sample at step 29 and hear any concern about the sole trader. Where a step says to tell the next role, a sole trader writes down the time and carries on.

3Before you start

The SDA Manager:

  • You can open REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist.
  • You hold the current NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (the still call it the SDA Price Guide) and the current SDA Design Standard, and you know their versions and dates: [Pricing Arrangements version and date]; [SDA Design Standard edition].
  • You have the list of laws for the dwelling's state or territory from REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.
  • You have access to the my NDIS provider portal (myID and RAM), where enrolment applications are lodged, and you know the NDIA contact for SDA enrolment: [NDIA contact for SDA].

Everyone who acts:

  • You have each resident's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, so you know how they want to be told things.
  • You know the repairs number, [repairs number], and the on-call number, [on-call number].
  • Workers: you know that any defect goes to the SDA Manager the same day (step 20).

4Watch out

  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A gas smell, smoke, a fire alarm going off, live wiring or flooding near power can kill. The defect report comes second.
  • Providing SDA in a dwelling the NDIA has not enrolled breaks a condition of our registration. It can bring a civil penalty (, section 6(a); NDIS Act 2013, section 73J). Nobody moves in as an SDA resident until the enrolment is on the row.
  • A signed certification must be true. Applying for a dwelling that does not meet the requirements also breaks that condition. The NDIA can cancel an enrolment after a notice of at least 14 days (SDA Rules 2020, section 27).
  • The density count includes other people's dwellings. A count of our own dwellings alone can leave a parcel over its limit, and our dwelling out of its enrolment.
  • The NDIA clock starts on the event, not on the day we find the paperwork. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment (SDA Rules 2020, section 29). The NDIA can cancel an enrolment for that.
  • A required design feature that stays out of use can change the dwelling's category. Residents lose the access the home was enrolled to give them. Fix it, and decide at once whether the NDIA must be told.
  • A lock, gate or sensor that limits a resident's movement may be a restrictive practice. Fit none without the authorisation the law requires. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies.
  • Entering a resident's home without lawful notice breaks and the resident's privacy. It also costs their trust in us.
  • A repair is never a reason to move a resident, or to change their supports. Housing and supports stay separate.

Before we apply to enrol a dwelling

Step 1

The SDA Manager

Open a dwelling row for each dwelling we think about enrolling.

Give it a dwelling code. Write the address and the owner. Note the of anyone who lives there now or may move in. A dwelling we manage but have not enrolled also gets a row. Nothing else starts until the row is open.

The shared areas, a bedroom and a bathroom meet the minimum design requirements for a category above basicNew buildSDA Rules 2020, section 8
It is not a new build. It is enrolled for 5 or fewer long-term residents, or for more than 5 from one family. The shared areas, a bedroom and a bathroom meet the minimum design requirements for a category. Between 1 July 2013 and 1 December 2016 it housed a resident with an extreme functional impairment or very high support needs who received a disability related support accommodation payment. That last test does not apply to the home of a participant who provides SDA to themselves. It is not a new build. It is enrolled for more than 5 long-term residents. The shared areas, a bedroom and a bathroom meet, or substantially meet, the minimum design requirements. Fits none of theseDo not apply. Stop and take adviceNot applicable

Decision table 3: density restriction (steps 8 and 16). The count is of eligible participants in every dwelling on the parcel, ours and other people's. When unsure whether to count someone, count them.

IfThen
The parcel has one dwellingThe restriction does not apply. Write "does not apply" and why
The parcel has 2 or more dwellings, and none of them is a new build or existing stockThe restriction does not apply. Write why
The parcel has 2 or more dwellings, and at least one is a new build or existing stockThe restriction applies. Work out the limit with the next three rows
The restriction applies, and any enrolled dwelling on the parcel is enrolled for 3 or more residentsThe limit is the greater of 10 eligible participants, or 10% of the bedrooms on the parcel
The restriction applies, every enrolled dwelling on the parcel is enrolled for no more than 2 residents, and the dwellings are part of an intentional community as section 31(3) defines itThe limit is the greater of 15 eligible participants, or 25% of the bedrooms on the parcel
The restriction applies, every enrolled dwelling on the parcel is enrolled for no more than 2 residents, and the dwellings are not part of an intentional communityThe limit is the greater of 15 eligible participants, or 15% of the bedrooms on the parcel
The count, with the person we plan to house, is more than the limitThe limit would be exceeded. Do not apply to enrol the dwelling. Do not fill the vacancy. Tell the Chief Executive the same day
The count, with the person we plan to house, is at or under the limitRecord the count, the limit and who you asked. We may go ahead

Decision table 4: the matters we certify and the evidence for each (step 11). The matters are in section 25(4) of the SDA Rules 2020.

MatterEvidence we holdStep that gets it
(a) The dwelling is permanent: fixed permanently to the groundThe certificate of occupancy, or its equivalent, and the certifier's description of the building10
(b) It is suitable to use for SDAThe accredited SDA assessor's final as-built certificate against the SDA Design Standard (new build), or the assessor's report against the Minimum Design Requirements in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (existing or legacy stock)6
(c) It will be long-term accommodation for at least one eligible participant, not respite, emergency or temporary useA note, by resident number, of each eligible participant it is for, with a statement that it is a permanent home7
(d) It meets all relevant building codes, standards and lawsThe certificates and approvals listed in the dwelling's rows, and the completed FRM-SDA-0310
(e) No complex home modifications funded or provided by the NDIS in the 10 years before the applicationThe owner's written statement and our own records9
(f) No other home modifications funded or provided by the NDIS in the 5 years beforeThe owner's written statement and our own records9
(g) The Commonwealth, or a State or Territory, does not provide funding in respect of the dwelling under a scheme unrelated to disability accommodationThe owner's written statement and our own records9
(h) It is suitable to house the maximum numbers of residents and of eligible participantsThe layout, the bedroom count and the assessor's comment7
(i) We have suitable capacity and experience to provide SDA thereOur registration for SDA, our workers, our systems and the upkeep budget12
(j) The owner has agreed in writing that we may enrol it, and that they will not enrol it separatelyThe signed agreement2
(k) The density restriction would not be exceededThe parcel record, the count and the limit8

Decision table 5: defect rating and time limits (steps 20, 21 and 22). AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement promises residents these times. Where the tenancy law of [state or territory] sets a shorter time, that time applies. A registered nurse must review the Emergency row's examples before first use.

RatingIf the defectMake safeRepair by
EmergencyRemoves power, backup power, water, a hoist, a call system or a way in and out from a resident whose support plan says they depend on it for breathing, feeding, suction, pressure care, medication or calling for help. Examples: a ventilator, oxygen concentrator, suction unit, enteral feeding pump or pressure-care mattress with no power; a resident who cannot leave their bed or room because a hoist or door opener is out of use. A registered nurse sets which failures are life-threatening for each resident, in the resident's planThe same day. Call 000 if anyone is in danger. Phone the on-call manager at once. The participant's medical emergency plan applies; the SIL provider and the participant's practitioner decide the clinical steps. Arrange interim power, equipment or a safe place within the hour where the plan requires itWithin 24 hours, or the interim measure stays in place and the SDA Manager reviews it with the SIL provider every day until the repair is done
UrgentPuts a resident's safety or security at risk now, or stops a resident using their bedroom, bathroom, toilet, kitchen or way in and out, where the Emergency row does not apply. Examples: a smoke alarm that does not work; exposed wiring; a gas smell; a structural danger; an external door or window that cannot be locked; no water, power or working toilet; a lift, hoist, door opener, call system or backup power a resident relies on that is out of useWithin 24 hours of the report, or another safe way to use the room or feature, agreed with the residentWithin 2 business days
HighLowers a resident's safety, security or privacy, or a fixture or feature does not work, but the home can still be used. Examples: a leak; a bedroom door that will not close or lock; a window that will not close; no window covering; a broken heater; mould; a trip hazardAn interim measure within 1 business dayWithin 5 business days
RoutineIs wear or damage that does not affect safety, security, privacy or useNone neededWithin 14 days of the report
Planned worksNeeds approvals, the owner's work, or a long wait for parts or a tradeAn interim measure for the whole waitTell the resident the date within 5 business days. The resident must agree to any date more than 14 days away. The Chief Executive approves any date more than 90 days away
Any ratingCannot be fixed within 10 business days, and affects a design feature, the structure, or the use of a bedroom, a bathroom or the way in and outKeep the interim measure in placeGo to step 25 the same day. Ask the participant's practitioner or an occupational therapist whether the dwelling stays suitable for each affected resident while the feature is out of use, and what interim measure is safe for them

Decision table 6: events the NDIA must be told about (step 25). The list is in section 29(1) of the SDA Rules 2020. The limit for every event is 5 business days (section 29(2)). Events (a) to (d) are notified under step 25 of this procedure. Events (e) to (g) are notified under PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) step 2, which owns them and uses this table for what to send.

EventThe 5 business days startWhat to send or doWho decides
(a) The design category or the building type has changedThe day it changedSay what changed and why. Attach the assessor's reportThe SDA Manager
(b) The dwelling is no longer suitable for SDAThe day we knowSay why, and what we will do for the residents. Take advice first if a resident could lose their homeThe Chief Executive
(c) Something has happened that is likely to change the category, the building type or the suitability. A required design feature that cannot be back in use within 10 business days counts. So does approved work that would change the categoryThe day it becomes likely. For a design feature, the day we know it cannot be back within 10 business daysSay what has happened and when it should be fixed. Attach any reportThe SDA Manager
(d) We intend to cancel the enrolmentThe day the Chief Executive decidesTell each resident first, in their format. Then tell the NDIA. PRO-SDA-05 covers any tenancy noticeThe Chief Executive
(e) An eligible participant has given notice to end their occupancy, or has been given The day the notice is given or receivedGive the date of the notice and the date the person leaves. Share the participant's identity only as far as the NDIA needs itThe SDA Manager
(f) A vacancy has arisen that an eligible participant could fillThe day it arisesSay which room and from when. Section 32 treats the person who left as still living there only if the NDIA has been told of the vacancyThe SDA Manager
(g) We propose to charge an eligible participant more rent than their SDA funding plus the reasonable rent contribution under the SDA Pricing and Payments FrameworkThe day we decide to propose itAttach a certificate from a qualified property valuer that the rent is fair and reasonable (section 29(3))The Chief Executive

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A resident says no to the inspection, or to a roomRespect it. Explain again what the inspection is for, and offer another time or a supporter. Write "not inspected" and the reason at question 6. Ask the resident or their supporter to test the smoke alarm and tell us. Never enter without lawful notice and agreement
A resident does not answer the notice, or is awayTry 3 times on different days, in the way they chose, and ask their supporter. Write each attempt in the entry record. After 3 attempts, tell the Chief Executive. The Chief Executive decides whether to use the lawful entry ground for a safety inspection under the tenancy law of [state or territory], with the full statutory notice, or to ask the tribunal; the attempts in the entry record show the auditor why. For an urgent defect, use the entry rules in the tenancy law of [state or territory]
The SDA Manager is awayThe Tenancy Officer acts, or the person named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. Certificates, NDIA deadlines and urgent defects keep their dates. The on-call manager takes urgent defects
The owner will not agree, will not answer, or will not fix a defectWithout the owner's agreement, do not apply to enrol. For a defect, write to the owner, copy the resident, and fix it ourselves after the due date, as step 22 says. Support a resident who wants to use their tenancy rights, or an advocate
A deadline will be missed: a repair, a certificate or an NDIA dateThe owner of the action tells the SDA Manager before the date passes. For an NDIA date, the Chief Executive asks the NDIA in writing for more time. For a repair, keep the interim measure in place and tell the resident the reason and the new date. Record both. A new date for an urgent defect needs the Chief Executive's approval
We find that something we certified was wrong, or that the dwelling never met its category or typeTell the Chief Executive the same day. The Chief Executive takes advice and tells the NDIA in writing within 5 business days (POL-SDA-04, ground rule 6)
More people live in the dwelling than it is enrolled forTell the Chief Executive the same day. Admit no one else. Never ask a resident to leave except by a lawful process. The Chief Executive takes advice, and tells the NDIA and the in writing within 5 business days (our standard)
The NDIA refuses an enrolment, or cancels oneThe Chief Executive decides the next step the same day. Tell each resident in their format, and offer an advocate. Their tenancy stays under tenancy law, and PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) covers any notice. Ask for a review where the law allows
A design feature fails and cannot be back in use within 10 business daysGo to step 25 the same day. Keep an interim measure in place until it is back. Tell each resident the new date
Fire, flood, storm or another event makes the dwelling unsafeCall 000 if anyone is in danger. Follow PRO-EDM-01 Emergency and Disaster Management Procedure. Help each resident reach safe shelter of their choice. Complete an incident report under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. Do not wait for an inspection to decide whether event (b) or (c) in Decision table 6 applies
A resident is hurt by a defectFollow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. The Quality Manager decides whether the incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission. Write the incident number at col P. Rate the defect urgent, or emergency where Decision table 5 says so
A resident complains about a defect, or about how we handled itFollow PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Keep the repair going. Nobody is treated worse for complaining
A lock, gate, sensor or other fitting limits a resident's movement or accessStop. Do not fit it, and tell the SDA Manager the same day. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies. Where one is already there, the SDA Manager checks whether an authorised behaviour support plan covers it. If none does, the Chief Executive decides what to do the same day, with advice
A worker or contractor entered without notice, photographed a person, or damaged a resident's propertyTell the SDA Manager the same day. The SDA Manager tells the resident, offers to put it right and records an incident. A concern about abuse or exploitation follows PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure
The concern is about the SDA Manager, for example a defect marked fixed when it is notTell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, tell the independent contact for concerns. You may also tell the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The owner sells the dwelling or ends our leaseTell the Chief Executive the same day. Residents keep their tenancy rights under the law. A new owner must give the written agreement in step 2 before we can keep the dwelling enrolled. The Chief Executive decides whether event (b) or (d) in Decision table 6 applies
An eligible participant wants to share a bedroomIt is their free choice. Help them tell the NDIA in writing (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)). Tell them that funding for the room depends on the NDIA agreeing that their needs are not adversely affected (section 24(1)(e)(ii)). Where the participant has a decision maker, take advice on who may make the choice before anything is sent. Write the date at col AG. Do not suggest it
The dwelling was enrolled before the SDA Rules 2020 startedThe law treats it as enrolled by the NDIA (SDA Rules 2020, section 41). Do not apply again. Open the dwelling row from the enrolment record you hold. Check its facts with steps 4 to 10 and step 19. Ask the NDIA to confirm the enrolled details in writing
The dwelling's feature list, certificate list or enrolment confirmation is missingDo not inspect from memory. Write "not known" with the date. Ask the NDIA in writing to confirm the enrolled details. Take the feature list from the design standard the dwelling was certified against: the SDA Design Standard edition on the assessor's certificate for a new build, or the Minimum Design Requirements in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation for existing or legacy stock. Ask the owner for each certificate. Build the lists, and set a date to finish them
A resident dies, or leaves without noticeFollow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure first. Then use events (e) and (f) in Decision table 6. Section 32 of the SDA Rules 2020 names a participant who dies, and needs the NDIA to be told of the vacancy. Do not enter or clear the room until tenancy law allows it and the family or the executor has been told
The system is downUse the paper form and the paper log. The SDA Manager enters the rows within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

An enrolled dwelling is ready for residents when all of these are true:

  • the NDIA has enrolled it, and its row shows the NDIA's reference
  • its building type, stock class, design category, bedrooms and enrolled maximums match the NDIA's confirmation
  • every matter we certified has evidence on file
  • its numbers and its density limit were checked before each move-in.

An enrolled dwelling stays compliant when all of these are true:

  • its last inspection and its last limits check are inside 6 months
  • every certificate and service on its list is in date
  • every defect has a rating, an owner and a due date
  • no emergency defect has gone past the same day, and no urgent defect past 24 hours, without being made safe
  • no other defect is past its Decision table 5 time, or past 14 days, without the resident's agreement
  • each event the NDIA must be told about was told inside the limit
  • every worker and contractor who works there has been briefed.

These records now exist:

  • the dwelling row, with its certified matters, application and the NDIA's decision, in REG-SDA-01
  • the completed FRM-SDA-03 for each inspection, with a row for each limits check, defect and entry
  • the certificate or service rows, each with its next due date
  • an NDIA matter row, with proof of sending, for each notice and answer
  • the briefing entries in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register and REG-HRM-03 Contractor and Supplier Register
  • the report every 3 months, with its actions in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register.

9Quick card

145 words
  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first, then report every defect the same day (step 20)
  • Never provide SDA in a dwelling the NDIA has not enrolled (step 15)
  • Check numbers and the density limit before anyone moves in (step 16)
  • Make an emergency defect safe the same day, and an urgent defect within 24 hours (step 21)
  • Tell the NDIA about each listed event within 5 business days; aim for 3 (step 25)
  • Answer an NDIA notice by the date it sets (step 26)
  • Never enter a resident's home without lawful notice: 7 days for an inspection, 2 business days for a repair the resident asked for, or longer where the law says; no notice only in an emergency (step 18)
  • Inspect every dwelling with its residents every 6 months (step 19)
  • Sign a certification only when every matter has evidence (step 12)

form.intro:
Use this checklist each time we inspect a specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling, with the people who live there. It checks the dwelling against its enrolment, the law and its state of repair.

The form has three uses. Complete only the questions each use names:

  • Enrolment check: every question, with Section B answered in full. The SDA Manager completes it before we apply to enrol a dwelling, with the reason "enrolment check before we apply".
  • Inspection: Sections A and C to I in full. Section B is pre-filled from the dwelling row in REG-SDA-01 before the visit, and the inspector confirms each item or writes what changed. The SDA Manager completes it every 6 months, and after a change, a defect, an incident or an NDIA request. The Quality Manager completes it for a sample re-inspection.
  • Defect report: questions 1 to 4 and question 40 only. Skip questions 5 and 6 and every other question. Any worker completes it the same day, for a defect found between inspections.

Phone first for an emergency or an . Call 000 first if anyone is in danger. The form comes second.

Have ready:

  • the dwelling's row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register
  • the NDIA's enrolment confirmation
  • the dwelling's feature list and certificate list
  • the last inspection
  • each resident's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.

What happens next: the SDA Manager enters the rows in REG-SDA-01 within 2 , and a repair row with its rating within 1 business day (the same day for an emergency or urgent defect), and tells each resident the result within 5 business days. PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure sets every step.

This form never ends a tenancy, never changes a support and authorises no restrictive practice. The question protocol uses two short names. The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to check that the dwelling meets its enrolment and the law, and that it is safe, secure, private and in good repair. It is about the building, not about how you live in it.

The SDA Manager, the , the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive see this form. The dwelling's owner sees only the defects, and only what they need to fix them. We share a resident's words with anyone else only with their consent.

We write no resident's name on this form. Each resident's own words go on their own file. We take a photo only with the resident's consent, and never of a person.

A resident can say no to any room. A resident can see what we hold about them and ask us to correct it. They use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form, or they ask any worker. Saying no, reporting a defect or asking for a correction never puts a resident's home at risk.
form.after:
• Worker: give a defect report to the SDA Manager the same day (our standard). Phone first for an urgent defect.
  • SDA Manager: enter the rows in REG-SDA-01 within 2 business days (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: rate each defect within 1 business day of the report, and the same day for an emergency or urgent defect. Make an emergency defect safe the same day and an urgent defect within 24 hours (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: tell each resident the result within 5 business days of the inspection (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: if question 42 is yes or not sure, tell the person Decision table 6 names the same day. The NDIA must be told within 5 business days of the event (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2)). We aim for 3 business days.
  • Quality Manager: read each inspection form in the monthly review.
  • If a deadline will be missed, tell the resident before it passes. Give the reason and the new date, and write both beside the question.
  • If the form is about the SDA Manager's own conduct, give it to the Chief Executive.
  • The form stays on the dwelling's file for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026) requires records of claims and supports to be kept for 7 years).

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each specialist disability accommodation () . It shows how we enrol it, keep it inside its enrolment, and keep it safe, secure, private and in good repair. Each row is one record about one dwelling. A row shows what was found or decided, who did it, which were told, and when the next action falls due.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 71 (1), s 71 (2) and s 71 (3).
  • The columns also evidence s 68 (1) and s 72 (5). FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request sends its rows here.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 6. , sections 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. , sections 5 to 8, 15, 19 and 24 to 32.
  • The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • No law sets the columns of this register. They are our standard, built from what the law makes us certify, notify and keep.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded. Keep a dwelling row for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years; this register's rows support SDA claims, so 7 years is also the statutory floor.
  • Other law can require a certificate or a safety record to be kept longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.
  • Roles and words: : the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. : the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the lives. : the dated list of state and territory laws kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

The register holds ten types of row. Column C names the type. Columns A to Q are the spine, and every row uses them. Each type then fills its own group of columns:

  • dwelling: columns R to AE
  • limits check: columns AF to AH
  • certificate or service: columns AI to AK
  • inspection: columns AL to AT
  • repair: columns AU to BA
  • modification record: columns BB to BG and BP to BT
  • entry record: column BH
  • matter: columns BI to BK
  • compliance check: columns BL to BM
  • house rules check: columns BN to BO

Residents' names are not kept here. A row uses . A resident number is the number we use in place of a name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register. Health details, behaviour support content and a resident's own words stay on their own file.

Keep each row type on its own sheet, with the spine columns first. A provider with one dwelling has few rows: one dwelling row, two inspections a year, and a handful of certificate or service rows.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification records, and may add a repair row from a resident's report. The Quality Manager adds compliance check rows, and inspection rows for a sample re-inspection. The person who enters a home records the entry the same day, and the Tenancy Officer adds the entry record. When the SDA Manager is away, the Tenancy Officer adds rows.
  2. Add the row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Add an NDIA matter row, a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and an emergency or urgent repair row the same day.
  3. Use one row for each limits check, certificate or service due, inspection, , modification request, entry and NDIA matter. An inspection that finds 3 defects makes 4 rows, plus a limits check row. Link them at col P.
  4. A dwelling has one dwelling row in force at a time. When a dwelling fact changes, add a new version of the row with the date, your name and the reason. The old version becomes "superseded".
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Write resident numbers, not names. Leave out health details, behaviour support content and a resident's private words.
  7. Use one row each time a certificate or a service falls due. When it is done, close the row and open the next one.
  8. When someone was hurt or nearly hurt, the event is also an incident. Write its number from REG-INC-01 Incident Register at col P. A complaint goes in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. A hazard to people while supports are given goes in REG-ENV-01 Hazard and Maintenance Register. Tenancy facts go in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. Link each one here.
  9. At any time, each must show a dwelling row with the status "enrolled". It must show an inspection row and a limits check row, each not older than 6 months. Its certificate or service rows must not be past their due dates, and no repair row may be past its due date.
  10. Reopen a closed row when the defect comes back. Set col N to "reopened" and write the reason.

A row is closed only when all of these are true for its type:

  • Dwelling: a new version has replaced it, or the dwelling is no longer enrolled with us and the NDIA has been told.
  • Limits check: the result is recorded. If it was "over a limit", the Chief Executive has decided what happens.
  • Certificate or service: the certificate or report is filed, and the next one has its own row.
  • Inspection: every defect has its own row, each resident has been told the result, and the next inspection date is set.
  • Repair: the work is done, someone other than the contractor has checked it, the resident says it is fixed, and the resident has been told. Any NDIA matter row for it is also closed.
  • Modification record: FRM-SDA-01 question 37 is answered.
  • Entry record: the visit is recorded, with the time out and any key used.
  • NDIA matter: the notice or answer was sent, proof is filed, and the NDIA's reply is recorded. A notice we sent may close on "no reply" after 20 business days (our standard). An application for enrolment, a request from the NDIA and a notice from the NDIA stay open until the NDIA decides.
  • Compliance check: every change found has an owner and a due date.
  • House rules check: every limit found is removed, or has its lawful authority and the Chief Executive's decision on file. Each resident affected has been told.

The SDA Manager approves closing. The Quality Manager approves closing for an urgent repair row, an NDIA matter row and a dwelling row.

• The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see the open defects, entry records and certificate rows for each dwelling where they work. They need these to work safely.
  • A resident can ask to see every row about their dwelling and about them, and can ask us to correct it. A resident sees other residents' rows only with names and details removed.
  • A dwelling's owner can see repair rows and certificate or service rows for their dwelling, limited to the owner view: columns A to H, K to O, AU (the defect category only), AV, AX to AZ, and the certificate or service columns AI to AK. They see no resident's details, nothing at col I or col J, and no resident number.
  • A contractor sees only the repair row for their job.
  • The NDIA, the , an auditor or a regulator sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows about a person's home hold sensitive personal information. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form or key log.

Photos show the defect, never a person. Take a photo in a resident's home only with their consent. Nobody keeps photos on a personal phone. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
